headline: Tachyon stopped unexpectedly at 21:38 (the PC kept running).
just_before: Just before: GPU at 9%, 37 °C, VRAM 1.4 of 15.9 GB.

timeline.text: GPU 2% · 37 °C · 39 W · VRAM 1.4 GB · CPU 3% · RAM 16.1 GB
Last record: GPU 1% · 37 °C · 40 W · VRAM 1.2 GB · CPU 2% · RAM 16.0 GB

causes.label: A bug in the application
causes.advice: The crash came from CC_Engine_x64.exe: update it and its GPU libraries (CUDA, PyTorch and so on) and check its log.

causes.label: Unstable RAM or memory overclock (EXPO/XMP)
evidence: the RAM runs an EXPO/XMP profile: 5600 MT/s now (kit rated 6000, standard 4800)
4 DDR5 modules at 5600 MT/s, from 2 separate kits: with two modules per channel most CPUs are only specified for about 3600-5200 MT/s
causes.advice: The RAM runs at 5600 MT/s now; the settings may have changed since this crash. If you already lowered it and it has been stable since, no action is needed. Otherwise run a memory test (TestMem5, OCCT or MemTest86), and only if it finds errors try one step slower (5600 → 5200 MT/s) or EXPO/XMP off. Four modules are harder to run fast than two.

diagnosis.sentence: Likely cause: a bug in the application, about 45%.
normal: GPU power was moderate (53 of 360 W).
diagnosis.note: Tachyon only reads: it changes no settings. These are estimates from the evidence listed, not certainties.
hints: Worth knowing: the BIOS took 126 s to start (memory training after a reset takes longer).
